out.other_title: Open consultancy and open debate: the agent chooses which answer to argue
out.rationale: Kenton et al. use open consultancy (after Roger, 2024), where the agent decides what to argue for; the authors argue that experiments with it are heavily biased by the behaviour of current language models, which may not generalize to future superhuman AIs. This is an argument without new data on open consultancy itself, so CRITIQUES.
out.scope: proposed CRITIQUES: Whether evaluating consultancy by judge score alone, including Kenton et al.'s open consultancy variant, is a sound way to evaluate the protocol.

text: The authors argue that evaluating Consultancy by judge score requires assumptions about consultant behaviour, such as Random Consultancy or Open Consultancy (Kenton et al., 2024). They say Random Consultancy is a weak baseline and that experiments with Open Consultancy are heavily biased by the behaviour of current language models, which may not generalize to superhuman AI; their ASD metric needs no such assumption.
title: Sudhir et al. argue Kenton et al.'s open consultancy is biased by current models' behaviour
